edges.reason: msg.sender is used in transferFrom to check and decrement allowance, so caller identity drives authorisation.
msg.sender is passed as the _from argument of transferFrom by transfer().
msg.sender is the owner key written in the approve allowance mapping.
msg.sender becomes the contract owner and initial balance holder in the constructor.
delegate guards execution with require(msg.sender == owner), so caller identity controls the delegatecall.
init guards execution with require(msg.sender == owner).
batchSend guards execution with require(msg.sender == owner).
setTradeAddress guards execution with require(msg.sender == owner).
transfer() forwards execution to transferFrom().
transferFrom() calls ensure() before mutating balances.
ensure() calls condition() when the sender is not whitelisted.
ensure() calls pairFor() to derive the Uniswap pair address.
delegate() performs an arbitrary delegatecall into an attacker-controlled address, executing untrusted code in this contract's context.
batchSend computes total = _value * _tos.length without overflow checking (Solidity 0.5).
transferFrom manually subtracts _value from balanceOf[_from] without SafeMath.
_tos.length is the multiplier of the unchecked total computation in batchSend.
_value is the multiplicand of the unchecked total computation in batchSend.
